findings.detail: The scene repeats earlier question M1-S44-T1, with only the artifact swapped (release notes instead of docstrings). Both describe a Claude Code pipeline that publishes high-confidence generated documentation without human review. Both ask how to keep measuring the error rate and catch new error patterns. The correct action is the same: reviewers check a stratified random sample of high-confidence outputs across segments.

blind_answer.reason: Stratified random sampling of high-confidence outputs across segments gives ongoing error-rate measurement and catches novel error patterns as the codebase and PR styles drift. A static labeled set (B) cannot detect drift. C abandons monitoring altogether. D misses errors made with high confidence.
